method: Official author GitHub release HTML/expanded_assets and raw author documentation; mGBA official downloads. Read-only metadata research: no builds downloaded or executed by this subagent.
globalNotes: These are native PS Vita packages, not PSP EBOOTs for Adrenaline.
No exact Vita firmware range is stated in the selected game READMEs; do not invent a minimum. A homebrew-enabled Vita with VitaShell is the installation prerequisite.
Do not describe repository build dependencies (VitaSDK/SDL development libraries) as dependencies users must install for a ready VPK.
VitaDB domain currently resolves to a domain-for-sale page. Use author URLs; do not offer its defunct service as a working download source.

entries.title: SuperTux Classic Vita
setup: Transfer the VPK and install with VitaShell; launch its LiveArea bubble. Game assets and LiveArea artwork are bundled.
Saves and configuration are managed in ux0:data/supertux/.
entries.data: Standalone free game; no commercial data needed.
entries.modelFirmware: Native Vita package. Author does not state an exact firmware range or a handheld model restriction; no independently verified PSTV statement found.

artwork.credit: SuperTux Team and contributors; PS Vita port theheroGAC. Original asset licensing follows SuperTux Creative Commons notices; software GPL-3.0-or-later.

entries.title: Jump'n'Bump
setup: Install the VPK with VitaShell. Multiplayer-only game, up to four controllers supported; Bluetooth keyboard controls are also available.
D-pad/left stick moves; action button jumps; Select/Start restarts or advances the results screen.
entries.data: Standalone; no separate data archive is documented.
entries.modelFirmware: Author provides native Vita build and notes Bluetooth keyboard support. No exact firmware minimum is published. Later release 1.01/1.02 changes affect Switch only.

artwork.credit: Screenshot from rsn8887's official port; original game Brainchild Design (Mattias and Andreas Brynervall, Anders Nilsson and contributors). Repository GPL-2.0.

entries.title: Enigma
setup: Install the VPK, then extract data.zip contents into ux0:data/.
Author recommends FTP for approximately 10,000 small files after a reported Mac USB transfer issue. Use stick or touch to guide the marble; D-pad left/right changes mouse sensitivity.
entries.data: Free game with supplied level/data archive; no commercial data needed.
entries.modelFirmware: Native Vita with touch and Bluetooth keyboard/mouse support. No exact firmware minimum or model limitation published. Versions 1.12–1.16 are Switch-only changes.

artwork.credit: Official rsn8887 Vita screenshot; Enigma developers Daniel Heck, Ronald Lamprecht and contributors.

entries.title: Chocolate Doom Vita
setup: Install VPK; extract data.zip at memory-card root ux0: (creates data/chocolate).
User-supplied full-game IWADs belong in ux0:/data/chocolate/iwads/. PWADs go in ux0:/data/chocolate/pwads/doom, heretic, hexen or strife as appropriate.
entries.data: Release data includes Doom and Heretic shareware. Full Doom/Ultimate Doom, Doom II, Final Doom, Heretic, Hexen and Strife require the user's own IWADs. FreeDoom also supported. A single VPK supplies the four game engines, not four independently counted apps.
entries.modelFirmware: Native Vita port. No exact firmware range/model restriction stated in README.Vita.md.

artwork.credit: LiveArea assets by tiduscrying, launcher graphics by KINGGOLDrus; Vita port fgsfdsfgs, Chocolate Doom contributors. GPL-2.0 project; game trademarks and original artwork remain their respective owners'.

entries.title: mGBA
setup: Extract the official Vita .7z on the computer, transfer its VPK and install with VitaShell.
Select your own GB/GBC/GBA game backups in the file browser. A user-chosen folder such as ux0:roms/gba/ is an organizational suggestion, not an upstream-mandated path.
entries.data: Emulator only, no commercial games supplied. Built-in BIOS implementation is available; original external BIOS files are optional.
entries.modelFirmware: Official site lists PlayStation Vita as a supported homebrew platform. No exact firmware minimum or handheld model restriction stated.

artwork.credit: mGBA project's official PS Vita icon; mGBA © Vicki Pfau and contributors, Mozilla Public License 2.0.

entries.title: Rocks'n'Diamonds
setup: Install VPK. Extract the matching data archive into ux0:/data/ so ux0:/data/rocksndiamonds/ contains the game's files.
Additional level folders go in ux0:/data/rocksndiamonds/levels/. Use binary transfer mode for FTP levelsets.
entries.data: Free game and supplied data; optional level pack is not needed for first use.
entries.modelFirmware: Author explicitly mentions VitaTV multiplayer up to four players; pair controllers before launching. No exact firmware minimum published. Versions 1.14/1.15 changed Switch only.

artwork.credit: Official screenshot by rsn8887; original game and graphics Holger Schemel and contributors.

entries.title: Mirror Magic
setup: Install VPK. Extract the matching data archive into ux0:/data/ so ux0:/data/mirrormagic/ contains the game's files.
Additional level folders go in ux0:/data/mirrormagic/levels/. Rotate mirrors to guide the laser before time expires.
entries.data: Standalone free game with supplied data archive.
entries.modelFirmware: Native Vita build from the same port project; no exact firmware range or additional model restriction stated.

artwork.credit: Official screenshot by rsn8887; original game and graphics Holger Schemel and contributors.
